dedupe_keys.name: heatsmart alliance home heat load tool

description: The Home Energy Analysis Tool estimates a dwelling's heat load and checks proposed heat-pump sizing. Its public code and README describe resident-provided historical fuel use, location, thermostat settings and nearby weather as inputs. The application returns heat demand against outdoor temperature and a comparison by floor area for the selected home. Geographic coverage is the homes whose residents provide data; the project names US utility examples. GitHub metadata states MIT licensing and the README links a live HeatSmart Alliance deployment. A limitation is that the original method comes from a spreadsheet and future features described in the README should not be treated as current functions. Historical fuel use and occupant behaviour can also distort the heat-load estimate. The tool can parameterise residential electrification scenarios for local energy networks. The related catalogue ERA5 record supplies weather context only. No resident data or web app files were downloaded.
inputs: Home fuel use, thermostat settings, location and local weather
name: HeatSmart Alliance home heat-load tool
notes: G7 G7-1658. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-28; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability.
outputs: Estimated heat load and heat-pump capacity comparison
provider: Code for Boston and HeatSmart Alliance
